bug_info.bug_desc: In the old read pipeline, when a flash read completed with a reliability ECC error, `muxed_err` became asserted but the read-buffer update was gated with `~muxed_err`. As a result, an allocated buffer entry that was in the `Wip` state never received its update, so it never transitioned to `Valid`. Transactions that matched this in-progress buffer were accepted and waited for that entry to become valid, causing the read pipeline to hang. Additionally, the `rd_buf_t` record had no `err` field, so the pipeline had no way to remember that a completed buffer entry contained erroneous data; future hits could match a bad entry and buffer responses could not report the stored error.
bug_info.fix_hint: Add an `err` flag to `rd_buf_t` and to the read-buffer entry module. Do not suppress the buffer update when `muxed_err` is asserted; instead, always update the buffer and capture `muxed_err` through a new `err_i` port. Clear the error flag on reset, disable, wipe, and allocation. Exclude entries with `err` set from buffer-hit matching so known-bad data is re-read from flash. When a response is selected from a buffer, propagate `read_buf[i].err` into `data_err_o` and gate `data_err_o` with `data_valid_o` so errors are only presented with valid responses.
